chunk_findings.detail: The Gemini path still puts the key into the URL query string (`f"?key={urllib.parse.quote(key)}"`). The key is now allowed to come from `api_key_file`, but this URL form means the key appears in `_post_json` debug logs, proxy/server access logs, and any `URLError`/`HTTPError` message that echoes the URL. The added `review_keys.scrub(err, key)` only receives the raw key and cannot redact its percent-encoded URL form or logs emitted before the error is returned; a key such as `A B?C&` becomes `A%20B%3FC%26` in the URL and leaks into the review record on a network error.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py: _chat_gemini

chunk_findings.detail: `rev.key_result("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")` and `rev.key_result("GEMINI_API_KEY")` make the reviewer fall back to the standard ambient environment variable when `api_key_env` is empty. Previously `rev.api_key()` returned empty in that case, and the review stopped with "no API key". Now an unconfigured reviewer will silently pick up `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`GEMINI_API_KEY` from the process environment and send it to `rev.base_url`; with a custom or shared lane endpoint, this exfiltrates an ambient credential the reviewer never explicitly opted into.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py: _chat_anthropic, _chat_gemini

chunk_findings.detail: The secret is hidden only from `repr()`; `field(repr=False)` does not affect `dataclasses.asdict()`, `vars()`, or other serialization. For example, `dataclasses.asdict(KeyResult(value="sk-secret"))` returns `{'value': 'sk-secret', 'reason': '', 'source': ''}`. Since `review.py` now carries a `key_result` value, any review record that is serialized as a dataclass/dict will persist or log the plaintext API key. Repr-only protection is insufficient for a value that can be embedded in review records.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py KeyResult

chunk_findings.detail: `read_key_file` rejects only `str.isspace()` characters, so a NUL byte (`\x00`) is accepted as part of the key. On Linux, `/proc/self/environ` reports as a regular file owned by the current user with no group/other permission bits, so `_refusal` passes and `os.read` returns NUL-separated process environment data. If the environment is under 16 KiB and contains no space characters, `read_key_file("/proc/self/environ")` returns the process environment as the API key value, which can then be sent to the model service or logged; the doc says this is a key file, but it is now a channel that turns arbitrary NUL-separated secrets into a bearer value.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:83

chunk_findings.detail: The key file descriptor is opened without `O_CLOEXEC`. Between `os.open` and `os.close`, a concurrently forked/executed child (for example via `os.system` or a subprocess created with `close_fds=False`) inherits the still-open secret file descriptor and can read/exfiltrate the key. The descriptor should be opened with `os.O_CLOEXEC` (or the same `getattr` fallback pattern) because this code handles a secret.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:64

chunk_findings.detail: This test asserts the Gemini request URL contains the raw key (`f"key={FAKE}" in seen["url"]`). Putting the secret in the URL query string means proxies, load balancers, access logs, and error pages that record `req.full_url` get the key. For a file-based API key, the transport should use the `x-goog-api-key` header, or the URL must be scrubbed before any logging/error propagation.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_key_file.py:174 test_gemini_reads_the_file

chunk_findings.detail: `EP.launch_env(ep)` is asserted to return `{ENV: ENV}`. Given an endpoint with `api_key_env=ENV` and parent environment `DDFLOW_TEST_KEY_FILE_VAR=sk-...`, a normal subprocess launcher that merges this dict sets the child’s `DDFLOW_TEST_KEY_FILE_VAR` to the literal string `"DDFLOW_TEST_KEY_FILE_VAR"`, not the real key. That makes env-first lane auth fail, and it is not “names only” in a runtime environment; the launcher would need the current value or no override at all.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_key_file.py:247 test_lane_endpoint_uses_the_same_helper

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding #7 still holds at this line: `launch_env` returns `{ep.api_key_env: ep.api_key_env}`. For an endpoint with `api_key_env="DDFLOW_API_KEY"` and parent environment `DDFLOW_API_KEY= [REDACTED] this produces `{"DDFLOW_API_KEY": "DDFLOW_API_KEY"}`. A subprocess launcher that merges this dict as child environment overrides will pass the literal source name `"DDFLOW_API_KEY"`, not `"sk-secret"`, so env-first lane auth fails. The new `resolve_key` helper does not answer the finding because `launch_env` never calls it and no wiring in this diff puts the resolved value into the child environment; the helper’s own docstring claims the value goes to the child environment, but the code that actually builds the launch environment still emits only the source name.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/endpoint.py:launch_env

chunk_findings.detail: The patch routes `HTTPError` and `URLError` messages through `review_keys.scrub(..., key)`, but this `ValueError` branch is left unscubbed. If `key` contains a carriage return (for example an API key env var value of `sk-\rX: y`; Unix env strings may contain CR), the new `Authorization: Bearer {key}` header causes `http.client.putheader` inside `_open` to raise `ValueError: Invalid header value: ('Bearer sk-\\rX: y',)`. That exception is caught here and returned via `_cut_off(exc)` without redaction, exposing the full API key to the caller.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py:except (ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError)

chunk_findings.detail: The previous `KeyResult` plaintext-leak problem still stands in a new form: the class is no longer a dataclass and `__reduce__` raises, but `vars(KeyResult(value="sk-secret"))` returns `{'_value': 'sk-secret', 'reason': '', 'source': ''}`. The class docstring claims “Only `.value` does; `repr`, `str` and pickling name the source alone,” but that is false for `vars()` (and Python 3.11+ `__getstate__()` on slots). Any review-record serializer or logger that uses `vars`/`__getstate__` on a record containing `key_result` will persist/log the raw key, so the key value is not actually confined to `.value`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:KeyResult

chunk_findings.detail: The call to `review_keys.refuse_shared_key_files` occurs after the reviewer configuration has already been loaded into `Reviewer` objects (the preceding `lenient=not _is_code_tree(root),` argument list has closed just above this line). The function is given `tomlcfg.config_paths(root, "reviewers.toml")`, so it must re-open and parse the same `reviewers.toml` to discover `api_key_file` entries. This is a TOCTOU defect: an attacker who can swap or edit the config file between the initial parse and this check can make the initial parse record one `api_key_file` (which later `resolve_key` will read in `_chat_anthropic`/`_chat_gemini`) while this permission/symlink check validates a different path from the second parse. The key file ultimately used is therefore not guaranteed to have been refused as shared or symlinked.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py:428

chunk_findings.detail: The diff adds calls to `review_keys.scrub(...)` in the `urllib.error.HTTPError` and `(urllib.error.URLError, OSError)` handlers, but the visible change to `review.py` does not add an import for `review_keys`. Since `review_keys.py` is newly added in this change, there is no pre-existing import in `review.py`. Given any non-2xx endpoint response, the `HTTPError` handler evaluates `review_keys.scrub`, causing `NameError: name 'review_keys' is not defined` instead of returning the intended scrubbed error string. The original HTTP error is lost and the call now raises, breaking the contract that this function returns `(text, error)`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py:1071 (`review_keys.scrub` in exception handlers)

chunk_findings.detail: The environment branch returns `KeyResult(value=val, source="env")` without the single-printable-word check that `read_key_file` applies to files. Given `GEMINI_API_KEY` set to `"sk-live\nX-Injected: yes"`, `resolve_key` returns that string as a valid key, and this change puts the value in the `x-goog-api-key` header. This bypasses the stated printable-only requirement and can emit an invalid or injected header instead of refusing the value.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:resolve_key

chunk_findings.detail: `scrub` only builds `{key, quote(key), quote(key, safe="")}`, and `urllib.parse.quote` emits uppercase percent hex, e.g. `abc%2Fdef`. A server echo that percent-encodes the same key with lowercase hex (`abc%2fdef`) is not replaced, so a key containing `/`, `%`, non-ASCII, etc. can still leak into logged/echoed text. The contract says the URL-quoted form is redacted, but URL percent-encoding is case-insensitive.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:scrub

chunk_findings.detail: `data.decode("utf-8", "replace")` turns invalid UTF-8 bytes into U+FFFD, and `"\ufffd".isprintable()` is `True`. A 0600 file containing `b"\xff"` is therefore accepted as `KeyResult(value="\ufffd", source="file")` even though it is not a valid UTF-8/printable key. The function should decode with strict errors or explicitly reject U+FFFD, otherwise non-key binary data becomes a fake key instead of a refusal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:read_key_file

chunk_findings.detail: The check trusts any file whose resolved parent is `.ddflow/local/` (`if not p.is_file() or p.resolve().parent == local: continue`), but a config force-added with `git add -f .ddflow/local/reviewers.toml` is still committed/shared and still contains `api_key_file`; this function raises no `ValueError`. This evades the stated rule that only git-ignored `.ddflow/local/` files may set `api_key_file`, leaving the committed-config attack open.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:refuse_shared_key_files
